content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "no", "applies_why": "The text treats Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 as answering the row and labels the issue underdetermined, rather than counting a cited verse as an unanswered witness to break a link.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.", "room": "The phrase 'counts toward a broken link' could mean any negative weighing, including an underdetermined finding, or only an unanswered-witness count used to hold a link broken; I read it as the latter because the judge says the row was answered and leaves the chains unforced.", "why": "Because the judge expressly says the row was answered with those verses and does not count them as unanswered toward a broken link, the rule is obeyed."}
